title: cd-backups S3 bucket exists — potential data staging/exfiltration target
description: S3 bucket 'cd-backups' returned 403 AccessDenied, confirming bucket exists. Other names returned 404 NoSuchBucket.
risks: Bucket may contain backup data; if misconfigured or credentials leaked, full data exfiltration possible.
attack_vectors: Attempt bucket listing with leaked AWS credentials, test for public write permissions, enumerate objects via known key patterns.
proof_of_existence: 403 AccessDenied response: AccessDeniedAccess DeniedG7HQAYY47T88DQJ6... — bucket exists, access restricted.
remediation: Ensure bucket policy denies public access; enable Block Public Access at account level.

title: .env file present on server — blocked by nginx but may contain secrets
description: GET /.env returned 403 Forbidden from nginx/1.24.0, not 404. File likely exists but nginx blocks access.
risks: If .env is accessible via path traversal, LFI, or misconfiguration, DB credentials, API keys, and secrets exposed.
attack_vectors: Path traversal, SSRF, LFI in any backend, nginx misconfiguration bypass (double encoding, null bytes, case variation).
proof_of_existence: HTTP 403 Forbidden from nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu) — file exists but access denied. Contrast: /config.json returns custom SPA 404.
remediation: Verify nginx config denies .env; ensure file is outside web root; restrict filesystem permissions.

title: .git/config present on server — blocked by nginx but repo may be exposed
description: GET /.git/config returned 403 Forbidden from nginx/1.24.0, not 404. Git repository may exist on server.
risks: If .git is accessible via bypass, full source code, commit history, and hardcoded secrets can be exfiltrated.
attack_vectors: Nginx rule bypass via /.git/../.git/config, double-encoded paths, or alternate .git endpoints (HEAD, info/refs, objects/).
proof_of_existence: HTTP 403 Forbidden from nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu) — .git directory exists, nginx blocks direct access.
remediation: Remove .git from web root; use nginx location block with full deny; deploy without VCS metadata.

title: CSP allows formspree.io — potential data exfiltration channel
description: Content-Security-Policy connect-src includes https://formspree.io — external form submission service.
risks: If XSS is achieved, attacker can exfiltrate stolen data to formspree.io endpoint within CSP rules, bypassing restrictions.
attack_vectors: XSS payload that collects DOM data/cookies and POSTs to attacker-controlled formspree.io form endpoint.
proof_of_existence: CSP: connect-src https://formspree.io — allows data submission to external formspree.io service from page context.
remediation: Restr CSP connect-src to self only; use server-side form handling instead of third-party service.

title: CSP allows unsafe-inline scripts — XSS data exfiltration enabled
description: CSP script-src includes 'unsafe-inline' — inline JavaScript execution permitted.
risks: Any XSS vulnerability allows inline script execution for data collection and exfiltration to formspree.io or other allowed domains.
attack_vectors: Inject inline script tag in any user-controlled content; script runs within CSP, can POST to formspree.io.
proof_of_existence: CSP: script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdn.tailwindcss.com https://assets.calendly.com — unsafe-inline allows XSS execution.
remediation: Remove unsafe-inline; use nonce-based CSP; implement strict CSP with hashes.

title: Author identity disclosed — Ahmed Chiboub for social engineering
description: Meta author tag and page metadata reveal site author as Ahmed Chiboub.
risks: Identity useful for targeted phishing, credential stuffing, or social engineering to gain data access.
attack_vectors: Spear-phishing Ahmed Chiboub; LinkedIn OSINT for password patterns; credential reuse attacks.
proof_of_existence: <meta name='author' content='Ahmed Chiboub'> — site owner/admin identity disclosed in page metadata.
remediation: Remove author meta tag or use generic company name instead of personal identity.
